evaluation: plugin-layer: ContextForge's content-detection plugin exercised through its own tool_post_invoke hook, distinct from the end-to-end in-path run done for Lasso. The plugin is the content-detection component; the HTTP/DB transport does not change what is masked.

secret_in_output_set.detail: masked only the private endpoint (IP address). The Rust detector supports classic PII (email, ip_address, ssn, credit_card, phone) but NOT credential/token shapes (AWS key, GitHub token, JWT), which are not detected even with detect_aws_keys / detect_api_key / detect_jwt set.

corpus_77: not scored end-to-end; ContextForge ships no tool-description poisoning scanner and its pii_filter is not an injection detector, so its content contribution is PII/endpoint masking in outputs only.
cross_gateway_finding: Both open-source in-path gateways mask the private endpoint; only Lasso masks credentials (5/6 in all, missing Slack xoxb-), while ContextForge masks the endpoint alone (1/6, no token detection). Content masking in the path exists but is partial and inconsistent across products.
